name: Nimacimab
lead: Nimacimab is an investigational monoclonal antibody that targets the cannabinoid-1 receptor (CB1) and is being developed for obesity and other metabolic conditions. Unlike earlier small-molecule CB1 blockers, it is designed to act on peripheral tissues rather than the brain, with the aim of avoiding the neuropsychiatric side effects that ended earlier drugs in this class.[1][2]

It has been registered in human trials in at least two settings: a small Phase 2 study in diabetic gastroparesis that began in 2019, and a Phase 2 obesity trial that began in 2024 and tests weekly nimacimab alone and together with semaglutide against placebo.[3][4] Published results from the obesity trial were not available in the sources reviewed for this article.
Nimacimab is not an approved medicine and is not an established part of appearance or fat-loss practice. It appears in this wiki because of interest in new anti-obesity drug targets.
infobox: Injection (weekly dosing in the registered obesity trial)[3]

paras: The endocannabinoid system, acting through CB1, influences appetite and energy balance. Earlier brain-penetrant CB1 antagonists lowered body weight but were limited by psychiatric adverse effects, according to the research literature.[1][2]

A 2026 preprint reported cryo-EM structures of human CB1 bound to nimacimab, alone and together with small-molecule orthosteric antagonists, and described a cooperative mode of inhibition that involves binding to the extracellular side of the receptor.[1] A 2026 review examined the rationale for peripherally restricted CB1 blockade in obesity and related metabolic disorders.[2]

A Phase 2 trial registered as NCT06577090, listed as active and no longer recruiting, enrolled about 136 participants with obesity and compares weekly nimacimab, and weekly nimacimab with semaglutide, against placebo. It started in August 2024.[3] No results from it were found.
An earlier Phase 2 study of nimacimab in diabetic gastroparesis (NCT03900325) was registered with six participants and began in 2019; its status is listed as unknown.[4]
No community material about nimacimab as an appearance tool was found. Interest in it is largely drawn from the broader discussion of new weight-loss drug classes beyond GLP-1 agonists.

timeline.event: Phase 2 study in diabetic gastroparesis registered.[4]
Phase 2 obesity trial, alone and with semaglutide, begins.[3]
Structural study and review of peripheral CB1 antagonists published.[1][2]

card.summary: An experimental anti-CB1 antibody for obesity that is still in Phase 2, with no appearance-use evidence.
card.note: Investigational only; no approved use and no published obesity results found.

quick.overview:
Nimacimab is an antibody drug that blocks the cannabinoid-1 receptor, a target involved in appetite and metabolism. It is being studied for obesity, including alongside semaglutide.

It remains experimental. The registered obesity trial began in 2024, and no published efficacy results were found.
quick.mechanism: It binds CB1 from outside the cell. Researchers designed it to work mainly in peripheral tissue so that it avoids the psychiatric effects seen with earlier brain-penetrant CB1 blockers.
quick.risks: Its safety profile is not established in published form. It is not approved anywhere and is available only within clinical trials.
